item.description:

item.title: Poles and Plants — Sat Sep 26, 10:00 AM — Johnston Mill Nature Preserve
item.description:
Join us for an educational hike about plants and hiking poles! During this hike you’ll join TLC Trail Guide, Nancy, to learn how and when to set the length of your poles, the most efficient way to grip your poles, and how to decide what features you want in your hiking poles. Along the way, TLC Trail Guide, Dale, will point out local tree and plant species you will see throughout the preserve. This is a great hike to build on both your hiking pole and plant ID skills!
This will be a moderate 2-3 mile hike over variable terrain, stopping periodically for educational moments. Another big thank you to Great Outdoor Provision Company and LEKI for letting us borrow poles for you to try, but if you have a pair already, please bring them! This is a free event, but preregistration is required.
If registration for this event is full, please fill out our waitlist form here, by September 24th at noon.

On this 1.4-mile hike, we will celebrate Public Lands Day by meeting our plant neighbors at TLC's newest preserve, Old Creedmoor. We'll amble along Lizard's Tail Loop identifying trees, shrubs, and herbs along the way. All levels of plant knowledge are welcome -- we are a community of learners and sharers!
This is a free event, but preregistration is required. The group will return to the parking lot by sunset, but please bring a flashlight or headlamp just in case visibility begins to lower at the end of the hike.
If registration is full, please fill out the waitlist form here by September 24th at noon.

item.title: Mecklenburg's Declaration: NC's Revolutionary Presbyterians — Wed Nov 18 — Presbyterian Heritage Center
item.description:
An article published in the April 30, 1819 edition of the Raleigh Register and North Carolina Gazette proclaimed the following: “It is not probably known to many of our readers, that the citizens of Mecklenburg County, in this State, made a Declaration of Independence more than a year before Congress made theirs. The following Document on the subject has lately come to the hands of the Editor from unquestionable authority, and is published that it may go down to posterity.”
The document in question was called the Mecklenburg Declaration of Independence, and it had allegedly declared Mecklenburg “free and independent” from British rule on May 20, 1775. Of the 27 men who were said to have signed the document, almost all were Presbyterian.
But many people were confused – why were they just now hearing about this revolutionary action? The original document burned in a house fire in 1800, and the published version had been reconstructed from notes made by the clerk of the 1775 meeting.

item.title: Community Stories: Sustaining North Carolina’s Black Heritage — Wed Nov 18, 10:00 AM — Gregg Museum of Art & Design
item.description:
Community Stories: Sustaining North Carolina’s Black Heritage at the Gregg Museum of Art & Design presents a series of vignettes exploring spaces of dignity, belonging, safety, and imagination within Black communities across North Carolina. Featuring historical photographs, contemporary images, artworks from the Gregg Museum collection including a handmade guitar by Freeman Vines, and ephemera from community partners, the exhibition reflects on place, memory, creativity, and spiritual resilience across generations. Through stories of triumph and adversity, Community Stories honors the ways Black Americans have sustained and uplifted their communities through family, entrepreneurship, cultural expression, and soulful imagination, while inspiring future generations.
Source: NC Cultural Resources

item.description:
Ballet BC transforms a theater full of strangers into a single, collective audience response—a gasp, a silence, a moment of awe.
This triple bill explores what it means to be human in relationship to one another, moving from the vulnerable to the virtuosic, exploring deeply personal stories and moments of quiet intimacy to the exhilaration of masses of bodies moving together as one.

In the Allenton gallery, Christa Capua’s “The Hours After Helene” is an ode to the Book of Hours, and finding strength after natural disasters, all through Capua’s unique southern futurism photocollage works. Upstairs in the Semans gallery, two artists share “Rooted in Joy”, which celebrates the botanical works of Kristin Gibson and Charisse Coleman. Gibson’s unique still life paintings which use the alla-prima painting method, and Coleman’s original eco-prints, highlight a love of nature, and urge the viewers to take a breath and enjoy. There will be light fare, drinks, and free activities.
